verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego... at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R5: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R3/R4/R6/R7: confirm Pacific off San Diego/California, April 10
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact location, date, and time of splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; repeated exactly in R2-R7
verifications.reasoning: All sources list the exact crew members with matching names and roles.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew completed a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day trip'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R4: 'officially as a 10-day mission'; R5/R6/R7: '10-day mission/journey'; R1 notes ~9.5 days but contextually 10-day
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as a 10-day mission, aligning with flight day counting.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission involved flying around the Moon without landing on its surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead... loop around it'; R3: 'free-return trajectory that featured a single loop around the far side'; R2/R4 confirm flyby no landing
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no landing, only lunar flyby/loop.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft landed safely in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'splashed down... perfect bullseye'; R5: 'parachute-assisted splashdown... safely extracted'; R3: 'perfect bulls-eye splashdown'; all confirm safe Pacific splashdown
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of safe splashdown in Pacific across sources.

verifications.claim: According to NASA officials, the Artemis II crew reached the farthest point from Earth (over 250,000 miles) any human has ever traveled.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'travel farther from Earth than anyone before them... 252,000 miles'; R2: 'record... 252,756 miles'; R3/R4: '252,756 miles... broke Apollo 13 record'; NASA officials confirm
verifications.reasoning: NASA/sources specify >250,000 miles (exact 252,756) as new human record.

verifications.claim: NASA and U.S. Navy personnel successfully extracted the Artemis II crew from the capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Navy divers... hoisted into Navy choppers'; R5: 'safely extracted... U.S. helicopters... USS John P. Murtha'; R6/R7: Navy recovery teams assist extraction
verifications.reasoning: Detailed accounts of successful NASA/Navy extraction post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is reported to be in good health.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'all four... feeling great, happy to be home'; R3: 'in good health and good spirits'; R4: 'all four astronauts in good health'; R5/R6/R7 confirm good condition
verifications.reasoning: Multiple post-recovery reports state crew in good health.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was a crewed test flight to prepare for future moon landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted... test their Orion capsule... making sure it's up to the task'; R3: 'shakeout cruise... fly crewed missions beyond Earth orbit'; R4: 'tested... crucial to... lunar landing'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe as crewed test to validate systems for future lunar missions.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned to land on the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis 3... send astronauts to Earth orbit... test docking... Artemis 4... put astronauts down near the lunar south pole'; R4: 'land on it in 2028' (implies later); R7: 'Artemis III... to Earth's orbit... test docking'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify Artemis III as Earth orbit docking test, not lunar landing; landing is Artemis IV/2028.
